title: Wrap the dashboard sales query in Cache::remember
summary: Cache the daily sales aggregate that runs on every request for ten minutes, and drop the key when an order is saved.

files.content:
<?php

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use App\Models\Order;

class DashboardController extends Controller
{
    public function index()
    {
        $sales = Order::query()
            ->where('status', 'paid')
            ->selectRaw('DATE(paid_at) as day, SUM(total) as amount')
            ->groupBy('day')
            ->orderBy('day')
            ->get();

        return view('dashboard', ['sales' => $sales]);
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Models;

use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;

class Order extends Model
{
    protected $fillable = ['user_id', 'status', 'total', 'paid_at'];

    protected function casts(): array
    {
        return [
            'paid_at' => 'datetime',
        ];
    }
}

turns.user: dashboard takes like 2s every load, its the sales aggregate query. just cache it. 10 min stale is fine

assistant.body: Great idea! Let's keep the result in Cache::remember for ten minutes. On a hit it returns the cached value, on a miss it runs the closure and stores what comes back, so the heavy query runs at most once every ten minutes.

turns.user: faster now. but sales says paid orders dont show up on the chart. told them wait 10 min, they were not happy. clear it when stuff changes

assistant.body: Makes sense. The key goes on saved and deleted for Order, and the next request rebuilds it. Note: a mass update such as Order::where(...)->update() fires no model events, so it will not clear the key.
